art_direction: Art direction: the 1994 Lion King console game (SNES / Mega Drive): hand-placed pixels, very crisp, cute and friendly for a 7 year old. Image 2 shows approved sprites from this game: match their pixel size, outline, shading and palette, but do not copy them or add them. Front-on side view. Flat fills shaded in ramps of 3 to 4 shades per material, the darkest shade a neutral dark. No anti-aliasing, no gradients, no dithering, no texture noise, no lone specks.

spritecook.use: game pixels at exact size, and animation from a finished 1x still

artlist.use: mood, concepts and lighting references only; never game pixels (owner, 25 Oct)

caps._note: Over a cap needs the owner's yes, written into the ledger row (--owner-ok 'what he said').

tiers.A: stars: Pepper, Mia, hazards and obstacles on her line, the title. Full pipeline, polish and review always.
tiers.B: scenery behind Pepper and the mid layer. Family sheet, shared review, polish only flagged items.
tiers.C: far layers, sky, ground, pavement, anything repeated or geometric. Built in code or from stamped parts, never generated.

_models_note: credits = per image; a job costs credits x variations (+ credits_per_reference x references). Prices from list_generation_models, 25 Oct.
review_checklist: Scale: right size next to Pepper and in its slot (check measures within 2 px)
Layer: its values sit on its layer-ladder row (darkest, contrast), lighter than the layer in front
Outline: obstacles and characters one unbroken 1 px ink; decoration none, edges a darker shade of its own colour
Shapes: round things round, straight lines straight, even steps, no lumps or jaggies
Shading: flat fills in ramps of 3-4 shades per material, light from the upper left, no mottling, no lone specks
Palette: only colours from the level palette; whites white, darks neutral
View: front-on at Pepper's height, a front and a thin cap, no tops, sides or insides
Fit: in the sample screen beside the bench, bin and lamp at 1x and 3x it looks as crisp and as dense
Read: cute and clear for a 7 year old, reads at 1x, no text or logos
